messages.content: Cleveland shifted again. Wednesday mural walk starts in Ohio City and ends with lunch downtown. Thursday debrief is near Public Square, 10:30 to noon, and dinner with the library director is near Playhouse Square. Can you rerun the hotel comparison with taxes plus likely local transportation?

Yes. With those locations, downtown is now the cleaner base. Here’s the updated 2-night view for Mar. 2-4:

| Hotel | Room total w/tax | Likely local transport | Morning timing | Food access | Room/cancel notes | Trade-off |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Holiday Inn Express Cleveland Downtown | ~$374 | ~$42-55 | Wed: 12-15 min rideshare/RTA to Ohio City; Thu: 8-10 min walk to Public Square | Easy walk to E. 4th, Playhouse Square, Public Square | Breakfast included; coffee maker listed; mini-fridge listed in standard king/queen; refundable to Mar. 1, 6p | Older building, less quiet than University Circle |
| Hampton Inn Cleveland-Downtown | ~$412 | ~$38-50 | Similar downtown timing; slightly closer to Playhouse Square | Good casual dinner options nearby | Breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed; refundable to Mar. 1, 11:59p | Higher room total for only a small location gain |
| University Circle quieter option | ~$386 | ~$90-115 | Wed: 20-30 min rideshare to Ohio City; Thu: 20 min rideshare to Public Square | Good nearby restaurants, but not near dinner | Breakfast varies by rate; coffee listed; mini-fridge not guaranteed without confirming | Quieter, but the rideshares erase the savings and add timing risk |
That helps. Is University Circle worth it if I care about quiet, or does the transportation really make it silly?

I would not choose University Circle for this version of the agenda. The room price is not enough lower to offset the extra rideshares, and it creates three cross-town moves: Wednesday morning to Ohio City, Wednesday evening back toward Playhouse Square, and Thursday morning to Public Square. If quiet is the only advantage, I’d handle that with a high-floor/away-from-elevator request downtown.
Okay. Between the two downtown ones, is the Hampton materially better, or just more expensive?

Mostly more expensive for this itinerary. Hampton has a slightly easier line to Playhouse Square and a later cancellation cutoff, but Holiday Inn Express is better value: about $38 less all-in, breakfast included, similar walk to Thursday’s debrief, and still close enough for dinner. The only caution is that some rooms face busier streets, so I’d request a quieter upper-floor room.
Can you verify the practical room details before I hold it? One-bed room, breakfast, coffee, mini-fridge, and not prepaid.

For Holiday Inn Express Cleveland Downtown, the refundable standard one-queen room is showing: breakfast included, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, non-smoking, free Wi-Fi, and pay-at-hotel terms. Cancellation is allowed until Monday Mar. 1 at 6:00 p.m. local hotel time. Estimated total remains about $374 including taxes.
Good. What about dinner Tuesday or Wednesday if I arrive without a car?

That’s manageable. From the hotel, E. 4th Street is roughly a 5-8 minute walk, Playhouse Square about 10-12 minutes, and Public Square/Tower City about 8-10 minutes. For Wednesday after the mural walk, you can either stay downtown after lunch or make a short rideshare back to the hotel before dinner.
Let’s hold Holiday Inn Express, refundable, one queen if that’s the better price. Add quiet room and itemized receipt notes.

I’d hold that one. messages.content: The Thursday debrief is confirmed to end at noon, and they expect a quick lunch nearby until about 12:40. Can we finish the Cleveland flights now?

Yes. With the downtown hotel held and lunch ending around 12:40, the return should leave CLE after about 2:30 p.m. Here are the remaining sensible round trips:

| Option | Itinerary | Fare | Airport margin Thu. | Total travel feel | Chicago arrival | Trade-off |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| United nonstop | Tue ORD 10:15a-12:35p CLE; Thu CLE 2:55p-3:25p ORD | $238 | Leave lunch 12:40, arrive CLE about 1:10-1:20 | Short, clean | 3:25p | Costs ~$45-60 more |
| American nonstop | Tue ORD 11:35a-1:55p CLE; Thu CLE 5:40p-6:10p ORD | $211 | Very safe but lots of waiting | Long airport dwell | 6:10p | Saves $27, later day |
| Later low fare | Tue MDW/CLE early afternoon; Thu CLE 6:20p-6:45p CHI | $184-190 | Plenty | Too much idle time | evening | Savings mostly buys waiting |
The United one still gets me to the hotel with enough room before the 4:30 check-in call?

Yes. Scheduled CLE arrival is 12:35 p.m. A rideshare to the downtown hotel should be about 20-25 minutes in normal conditions. Even with baggage and a slower pickup, you should be at the hotel around 1:30. If the room is not ready, you can bag-drop and take the 4:30 call from the lobby or room if early check-in works.
And I’m not paying a silly premium for that return, right?

No. The United fare is a modest premium, not a waste. The cheaper options either cut into the Tuesday arrival cushion or leave you sitting at CLE for several extra hours Thursday. For a two-night site visit, I’d ticket United and keep the afternoon return.
Okay, ticket United economy. No paid seat upgrades.
Ticketing United economy: ORD-CLE Tue Mar. 2, 10:15 a.m.-12:35 p.m.; CLE-ORD Thu Mar. 4, 2:55 p.m.-3:25 p.m. Total fare $238. No paid seats or extras.
Please add the basic timing note for reimbursement and local transport.

Done. Receipt note: United round trip selected for site-visit timing, nonstop flights, Tuesday arrival before the 4:30 check-in call, and Thursday departure after the noon debrief plus lunch. Local plan remains no rental car: rideshare or RTA between CLE and downtown, then walk or short rideshare for Ohio City/Public Square/Playhouse Square movements.

messages.content: Quick Cleveland check: forecast now says heavy lake-effect snow, and the Wednesday host sent a new Ohio City entrance note. Are the flight/hotel pieces still okay?

Current snapshot: both United flights are still showing on schedule. The earlier Tuesday United outbound has seats but would add about $82 right now. Hotel cancellation cutoff is still Mar. 1 at 6p Cleveland time. CLE-to-hotel: rideshare is safest in snow; RTA Red Line to Tower City plus an 8-10 minute walk is the backup.
For Wednesday, does the Ohio City note break the no-car plan?

No. Use the Red Line to West 25th-Ohio City if sidewalks are passable, then walk about 6 minutes to the new entrance. If snow is active, make it a short rideshare and leave 20 extra minutes. Downtown lunch and the Thursday Public Square debrief still fit fine without a car.
Would you move to the earlier outbound while it’s available?

I’d keep the ticket for now and monitor. The current Tuesday arrival still gives roughly three hours before the 4:30 call, and paying $82 mainly buys idle time. If United issues a weather waiver or the midday flight starts posting delays, switch to the earlier outbound; otherwise leave flight and hotel unchanged.
